It's all consumer driven. While I take offense with OP's trashing of piles/retro games, I understand the underlying sentiment. A lot of crap is getting released these days, and it is not all pixel games. I have a ridiculous number of games in my steam library, mostly indies. While I am usually careful and read the reviews, I have bought junk games before.

It's the app market effect/idiocracy/f2p effect. It happens to big developers and indie makers alike, but it's usually more prominent among indies. People expect free games anymore. You may spend 2 years making a great game, then nobody buys it. So next time, rather than wasting two years making an awesome game that consumers just won't purchase, you spend a few months on some lowest common denominator level retardtainment like flappy bird. It's as surprise hit, made you a lot of money and a sequel is already planned.

Why should developers waste a lot of time making awesome games that all the smart people are too cheap to buy when you could make something quick and stupid for the masses and make a ton of money?

With that said, I know why I do it. I work on my projects for different reasons. I want to make a great game, pure and simple. That why I'm willing to spend 3 years on a project. It's my passion, not my job, and I have the luxury of other income to allow me that.

I love a lot of those retro games OP was trashing. They aren't all junk, and a savvy enough consumer know how to find the gems without wasting money on garbage. You just have to look for games that the developers put time and passion into.

Is the flood of junk games right or wrong? I don't know. It's the invisible hand of the free market. It hurts the folks making good games. Makes it a lot harder to stand out and get noticed. But it's the market.

I hope that, when I finally finish my game and try to sell it,I can make decent money from it. It only helps me when it's time for the next project. My fear is, and it's much more likely that, the game won't get enough attention to sell no matter how good it is. I will have wasted several years making a gem where I could have far surpassed my financial expectations making several lumps of coal to sell instead. I don't know what I'll do at that point.
